event.what_happened: The Fed held its rate at 3.75% to 4.00% on 2026-10-28 with two members voting for an increase. Its minutes say futures markets put high odds on a quarter-point rise by year-end and two more by summer 2027. PCE inflation was 3.6% in September and 3.8% in October.
event.how_it_reaches_markets: Higher discount rates for equities; tighter financing conditions; pressure on highly indebted borrowers.

sourced_facts.text: 2026-10-28: the FOMC kept the federal funds target range at 3-3/4 to 4 percent by a 10-2 vote; the two dissenters preferred a quarter-point increase; the statement says inflation remains elevated

Minutes of that meeting: futures prices assigned 'high probabilities' to 'a 25 basis point hike by year-end and two more by the summer of 2027'; 12-month PCE inflation 'rose to 3.6 percent in September', core 3.1 percent

October 2026 CPI (released 2026-11-10): all items +0.4% on the month, core +0.3%, seasonally adjusted. BLS did not publish 12-month changes for October because October 2025 data are missing after the 2025 appropriations lapse

October 2026 PCE price index (released 2026-11-25): up 3.8 percent from the same month one year ago and 0.3 percent from the preceding month; excluding food and energy, up 3.3 percent from one year ago and 0.3 percent on the month. The next release is 2026-12-23

history.note: Card opened. Resolution conditions written before the outcome is known.

Sources upgraded. The policy rate and the dissents now come from the Federal Reserve statement and the monthly price change from the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Market-implied odds and the 2026-11-25 data wording were moved to unconfirmed_facts.

Second pass. The market-implied path of rate increases and September PCE inflation were confirmed in the FOMC minutes. A reading note was added because BLS published no 12-month CPI change for October 2026, which the first resolution condition relies on.

Summary rewritten so that it states only what was confirmed at the listed sources and marks the rest as reported. The first version is kept under superseded_sources. Resolution conditions are unchanged.
Added numeric_criteria (version 1: how each condition is counted, with the latest reading) and counter_view (why this reading may be wrong). Resolution conditions are unchanged.

Added October PCE inflation (3.8%, core 3.3%) from the Bureau of Economic Analysis release of 2026-11-25, to the facts and the summary. The matching unconfirmed line now covers only the Q3 growth revision. Resolution conditions and numeric criteria are unchanged: they count CPI, not PCE.
Added forecast 1: by 2027-03-31, 5% resolved, 10% worsened. Scored in public (forecasts/README.md). Conditions unchanged.

unconfirmed_facts: 2026-11-20: CME FedWatch 92% chance of a December hike: from a broker commentary; CME itself not read. The Fed minutes above support the direction but not this number

2026-11-25: Q3 growth reported as revised up: the release behind this wording has not been identified. (The October inflation part of the same report is now confirmed above, from the Bureau of Economic Analysis.)

notes: 'Signal no further hikes' counts when the FOMC statement drops its reference to possible further increases, or when the median projection shows no higher rate at the end of the following year than the current range.
Year-over-year CPI: months for which BLS publishes no 12-month change (October 2026 is one) are skipped; the condition uses the two most recent months that do have a published figure.

items.measure: One FOMC statement without a reference to possible further increases, or a median projection showing no higher rate at the end of the following year than the current range
items.latest: 0 of 1. On 2026-10-28 the range was held at 3.75% to 4.00% with 2 of 12 votes for an increase

items.latest: 0 of 2. No 12-month figure was published for October 2026

counter_view.text: The Fed's own minutes say futures already put high odds on a rise by year-end and two more by summer 2027. A rise that is already in prices may add little new stress, and oil has come down from its October level.

worsened_when_any: The Fed raises by more than 0.25 percentage points at one meeting
